about: Every source the Ocean Data Initiative (and the Bermuda Standard's climate engine) reads, or is preparing to read. live=true: fetched every week by the QEM. live=false: listed, with a reader still to build or access still to arrange. Being listed is not trust: every reading starts unlit and brightens only when independent sources agree. Built from hub-culture/qem sources/registry.json by scripts/build_sources.py.

sources.name: NOAA CO-OPS (Tides and Currents)
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105).
sources.about: Water temperature measured by tide-gauge sensors, hourly.

sources.name: Open-Meteo Marine Weather API
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, crediting Open-Meteo.com. The free API is for non-commercial use; commercial use needs an API plan.
sources.about: Sea surface temperature from ocean models, hourly, at the nearest sea grid cell. A model, not a gauge. Open-Meteo's own documentation credits its sea surface temperature to the Copernicus Marine Service's global model (doi:10.48670/moi-00016, Mercator Ocean), so its lineage is mercator: it is the same model as the copernicus-marine source, passed through Open-Meteo, never an independent voice beside it.

sources.name: Marine Institute Ireland (Irish Weather Buoy Network)
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, crediting the Marine Institute.
sources.about: Hourly sea temperature from the M-series weather buoys off Ireland, via the Institute's ERDDAP server. An independent gauge network, so it triangulates against Open-Meteo just as NOAA does.

sources.name: Argo floats (via Ifremer ERDDAP)
sources.licence: Argo data are free and unrestricted; cite Argo (doi:10.17882/42182).
sources.about: Near-surface (top 10 dbar) temperature from profiling floats in the western North Atlantic, one reading per profile. A moving gauge: each profile is its own place, paired with Open-Meteo at the float's position and hour.

sources.name: Argo floats off Africa (via Ifremer ERDDAP)
sources.licence: Argo data are free and unrestricted; cite Argo (doi:10.17882/42182).
sources.about: Near-surface (top 10 dbar) temperature from profiling floats in the eastern Atlantic off Africa, from the Canary Current off Morocco to the Benguela off Namibia and South Africa, one reading per profile. The same Argo programme and reader as the western floats, in a box of its own.

sources.name: PIRATA moored buoys (NOAA PMEL, via PMEL ERDDAP)
sources.licence: Free and open, crediting the GTMBA Project Office of NOAA/PMEL.
sources.about: Daily mean sea surface temperature (1 m) from the PIRATA moored buoys in the tropical Atlantic, run by Brazil, France and the US (NOAA PMEL). The three in the eastern Atlantic are the open, current sea-temperature sensors on the African side. A daily gauge: its daily mean is weighed against MUR and the model's daily mean, never against a single model hour. A few days late; the weekly gap fill catches up.

sources.name: NOAA NCEI OISST v2.1 (near real time)
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain.
sources.about: Daily 0.25° sea surface temperature blended from satellites, ships and buoys, at each place. The near-real-time product appears a day or two late, so each day's snapshot holds the analysis of two days before; readings carry OISST's own date. Stored on the line but not used to triangulate: it shares NOAA's lineage with the CO-OPS gauges and may assimilate the same buoys. Coastal places whose grid cell OISST counts as land get no value.

sources.name: NASA/JPL MUR SST v4.1 (via NOAA CoastWatch ERDDAP)
sources.licence: NASA open data, free to use with attribution (JPL MUR MEaSUREs Project, doi:10.5067/GHGMR-4FJ04).
sources.about: Daily 0.01° (about 1 km) sea surface temperature analysis from satellites, at each place. Independent of NOAA's gauges and of Open-Meteo, so it's the third voice in a daily check: each place's gauge daily mean is weighed against MUR and the model's daily mean. It appears about two days late, so each snapshot asks for two days before. Places on cells MUR counts as land get no value.

sources.name: NOAA Coral Reef Watch 5 km (via PacIOOS ERDDAP)
sources.licence: NOAA near-real-time product, public domain. The dataset also carries a Met Office OSTIA academic-only statement, which covers only its 1985-2002 reanalysis; the QEM fetches current days only.
sources.about: Daily coral bleaching heat stress at reef sites: Coral Reef Watch's own Bleaching Alert Area level (No Stress, Watch, Warning, Alert Level 1, Alert Level 2), Degree Heating Weeks, HotSpot and SST anomaly. Heat stress is only meaningful over reefs, so it's fetched for the reef sites, not every place. Two days late, like OISST.

sources.name: OBIS (Ocean Biodiversity Information System)
sources.licence: Per dataset: CC0, CC BY or CC BY-NC, carried on each speck.
sources.about: Species occurrence records within 0.25° of each place. Records reach OBIS months after they're made, so each day's snapshot takes the records dated exactly one year before it. Names of people (recordedBy, identifiedBy, rightsHolder) are dropped. Each record keeps its dataset's own licence; records without one, or that OBIS's checks dropped, are skipped.

sources.name: World Bank World Development Indicators
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, crediting the World Bank.
sources.about: Marine protected areas as a share of territorial waters, by country and year (ER.MRN.PTMR.ZS), for every Atlantic Rim country. Compiled by the World Bank from the WDPA.

sources.name: UN Global SDG Indicators Database
sources.licence: UN data, free to use with attribution to the UN Statistics Division, Global SDG Indicators Database.
sources.about: SDG indicator 14.5.1: average share of marine Key Biodiversity Areas covered by protected areas, by country and year, for every Atlantic Rim country.

sources.name: Our World in Data
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, crediting Our World in Data and the producer named on each chart (FAO; Global Carbon Project). Third-party data keep their own licence; the API answers 403 for data that can't be redistributed.
sources.about: Country context for the Atlantic Rim from Our World in Data's chart API (ourworldindata.org/grapher/<slug>.csv, with <slug>.metadata.json beside it): wild-catch and farmed fish production and seafood eaten per person (FAO), and CO2 emissions per person, by consumption and cumulative (Global Carbon Project). OWID passes these producers' data on, so each value carries its producer as its upstream lineage and is never an independent voice beside that producer. Marine protected areas are left out: OWID's figures are the World Bank's, which wb-indicators already reads. Indicator specks stay on the line.

sources.name: World Bank Projects & Operations
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, crediting the World Bank.
sources.about: World Bank projects in Atlantic Rim countries tagged with the Oceans or Coastal Zone Management theme: name, country, status, approval date and total commitment. The commitment is the whole project's, not only its ocean share.

sources.name: IATI Datastore (International Aid Transparency Initiative)
sources.licence: Open data published by each reporting organisation under its own licence (most CC BY or ODbL); accessed through the IATI Datastore API under IATI's terms of use.
sources.about: Aid and development activities in Atlantic Rim countries that are in the fishing sector (DAC 313) or whose title mentions the ocean, marine or coastal work, fisheries, coral, mangroves or the blue economy; pipeline and active only. Each records its donor, recipient countries and dates. Amounts are left out: donors report in their own currencies and share activities across countries and sectors.

sources.name: Marine Regions EEZ boundaries (VLIZ)
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, crediting Flanders Marine Institute (VLIZ), Marine Regions.
sources.about: The boundaries of the EEZs the places and reefs lie in, from the Marine Regions WFS, simplified to about 0.01 degrees (around 1 km) for maps. The base layer other layers roll up by.

sources.name: Wikipedia (English)
sources.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0, crediting Wikipedia contributors; derivatives share alike.
sources.about: Lead sentences of chosen articles, each pinned to the exact revision it came from. A tertiary source: a sentence citing NOAA is NOAA's lineage, not an independent one.

sources.name: Global Fishing Watch APIs
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: Fishing, encounter and port events from AIS. Free API token on registration; data CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial without an agreement).

sources.name: Ocean Networks Canada (Oceans 3.0 API)
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: Cabled observatory sensors off British Columbia. Free token from an ONC account. A good next independent gauge network.

sources.name: Copernicus Marine Service (Global Ocean Physics Analysis and Forecast)
sources.licence: Copernicus Marine Service licence: free, worldwide, royalty-free and perpetual; redistribution must credit "Generated using E.U. Copernicus Marine Service Information" with the product DOI, doi:10.48670/moi-00016. The service commits to free access until 30 June 2028.
sources.about: Hourly sea temperature at 0.5 m from Mercator Ocean's global model at 1/12°, at every place and Argo position, from the nearest sea cell within 0.15°. The primary source of the sea surface temperature Open-Meteo serves, so it shares Open-Meteo's lineage (mercator) and is not an independent second model: the three-source hourly check stays silent until a model of another lineage joins. Read with the official copernicusmarine toolbox (scripts/fetch-copernicus.py), with a free account whose login comes from COPERNICUSMARINE_SERVICE_USERNAME and _PASSWORD.

sources.name: EMODnet Physics (ERDDAP)
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: European in-situ moorings and buoys on an open ERDDAP server (erddap.emodnet-physics.eu). Answers today; adapter not written yet.

sources.name: Australian Ocean Data Network / IMOS
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: Australian moorings and buoys via an open GeoServer (WFS). The homepage timed out from here but the GeoServer answers; adapter not written yet. IMOS (imos.org.au) delivers its data through AODN.

sources.name: NOAA World Ocean Database
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: Quality-controlled historical profiles, public domain. Bulk files, not a daily query API: suited to a one-off historical import.

sources.name: NOAA Fisheries (FOSS landings)
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: Annual commercial and recreational landings by state and species (apps-st.fisheries.noaa.gov/ods/foss). Open; yearly, so not part of the daily fetch.

sources.name: ICES data services
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: Fish survey (DATRAS) and vocabulary web services, open. Survey data are periodic; adapter not written yet.

sources.name: SeaDataNet
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: Pan-European data infrastructure; restricted data need a Marine-ID account. Portal-style access.

sources.name: British Oceanographic Data Centre
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: UK archive incl. tide gauges; downloads need registration.

sources.name: Marine Data Exchange (The Crown Estate)
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: Survey data from UK offshore industry; download portal with registration.

sources.name: NASA SeaBASS
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: In-situ bio-optical archive (file downloads). OCF links to www.seabass.gsfc.nasa.gov, which doesn't resolve.

sources.name: AquaMaps
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: Modelled species distribution maps; no public API; CC BY-NC.

sources.name: OpenSeaMap
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: Nautical map tiles and seamarks (ODbL). Map layers, not observations.

sources.name: IODE Ocean Data Portal / ODIS
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: A catalogue of other providers' datasets. Useful for discovering sources, not a source of readings.

sources.name: MarineTraffic
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: Vessel positions (AIS). Paid API only; blocks automated requests.

sources.name: Sinay
sources.licence: See provider terms.
sources.about: Commercial maritime data platform. Paid API only.

sources.name: NOAA GML Mauna Loa CO2 (daily)
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain.
sources.about: Daily mean CO2 in air at Mauna Loa Observatory, NOAA's continuous analyser. Read for the 60 days before each snapshot.

sources.name: Scripps CO2 Program, Mauna Loa (daily)
sources.licence: Free to use with credit to the Scripps CO2 Program (Keeling et al.).
sources.about: Daily baseline CO2 at Mauna Loa from Scripps's own in situ analyser, the Keeling record. A separate instrument and calibration from NOAA's, so a separate lineage at the same place. Its files are updated every few weeks.

sources.name: NOAA GML flask CO2, Tudor Hill, Bermuda (BMW)
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain.
sources.about: Monthly CO2 from air samples collected at Tudor Hill, Bermuda since 1989: Bermuda's own record. No second lineage samples Bermuda, so it is on the line, not checked.

sources.name: NOAA GML global CH4 (monthly)
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain.
sources.about: Global monthly mean methane from NOAA's marine surface sites. On the line until a second lineage (AGAGE) is added.

sources.name: NASA GISTEMP v4
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain.
sources.about: Global monthly surface temperature anomaly (land GHCN stations and ERSST ocean), on 1951-1980; rebased by the QEM to 1991-2020. NOAA GlobalTemp uses the same inputs, so it would add no lineage.

sources.name: Met Office Hadley Centre / CRU HadCRUT5
sources.licence: Open Government Licence v3, crediting the Met Office Hadley Centre and the Climatic Research Unit.
sources.about: Global monthly surface temperature anomaly (CRUTEM land and HadSST ocean), on 1961-1990; rebased by the QEM to 1991-2020.

sources.name: Berkeley Earth Land + Ocean
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, crediting Berkeley Earth.
sources.about: Global monthly surface temperature anomaly from Berkeley Earth's high-resolution (0.25°) product, rebased by the QEM to 1991-2020. Its ocean part is a reinterpolated HadSST, so over the sea it is not fully independent of HadCRUT5. Berkeley Earth stopped updating the classic 1° Land_and_Ocean_complete.txt in Q2 2025 (it ends at December 2024); the high-resolution file replaced it (switched 13 November 2026). Berkeley Earth labels it experimental and subject to revision.

sources.name: Copernicus Climate Change Service ERA5 (Climate Pulse)
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, crediting the Copernicus Climate Change Service / ECMWF.
sources.about: Daily global 2 m air temperature anomaly on 1991-2020 from the ERA5 reanalysis, averaged by the QEM over each complete month. A reanalysis, so a different method from the station records.

sources.name: NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4
sources.licence: Free to use with credit to NSIDC (Fetterer et al., G02135).
sources.about: Daily sea ice extent for the Arctic and the Antarctic from passive microwave satellites. Read for the 60 days before each snapshot.

sources.name: EUMETSAT OSI SAF Sea Ice Index v3
sources.licence: Free to use with credit to EUMETSAT OSI SAF.
sources.about: Daily sea ice extent for both hemispheres from EUMETSAT's own sea ice concentration records: a different algorithm from NSIDC's, reading 0.3 to 0.4 million km² higher on average.

sources.name: NOAA CO-OPS air temperature, St George's, Bermuda
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain.
sources.about: Hourly air temperature at the St George's Island tide station (2695540). The station has no water temperature sensor.

sources.name: Bermuda Weather Service METARs, L.F. Wade International (TXKF), via aviationweather.gov
sources.licence: Public domain as distributed by the NOAA Aviation Weather Center.
sources.about: Hourly routine aviation reports from Bermuda's airport, in whole degrees: the last 72 hours at each snapshot.

sources.name: Open-Meteo Historical Forecast API, ECMWF IFS
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, crediting Open-Meteo.com. The free API is for non-commercial use.
sources.about: Hourly 2 m air temperature at Bermuda from ECMWF's IFS model, asked for by name so it can't fall back to NOAA's GFS. A model, not a gauge.

sources.name: Climate TRACE assets (mining and waste)
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Climate TRACE).
sources.about: Mines, quarries, landfills and waste incinerators in the Atlantic Rim countries, with each asset's estimated emissions (t CO2e, 100-year GWP), activity, capacity and owners, and Climate TRACE's own confidence in each figure. These are modelled estimates from satellites and other remote sensing, not reported measurements. Read for the year two before the snapshot, the latest Climate TRACE treats as complete.

sources.name: US EPA Toxics Release Inventory
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain.
sources.about: Toxic chemical releases reported by industrial facilities in the US Atlantic and Gulf coast states, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands: one speck per facility, chemical and year, with total on-site and off-site releases, the facility's position and sector, and whether the chemical is a carcinogen. Self-reported by the facilities to the EPA. Read for the year two before the snapshot, the latest the EPA has published.

sources.name: NOAA AOML sargassum (AFAI, 7-day)
sources.licence: NOAA AOML OceanWatch: may be used and redistributed for free but is not intended for legal use.
sources.about: The Alternative Floating Algae Index, a 7-day composite from satellite ocean colour, in a small box around each place: the mean and the highest value of the clear cells and how many cells were clear. AFAI rises with floating sargassum; it says how much floating algae a satellite saw, not how many tonnes reached a beach, and no threshold is claimed here.

sources.name: NOAA NCEI Marine Microplastics
sources.licence: US Government work (NOAA NCEI compilation), public domain; each study under its own terms.
sources.about: Microplastics samples from published studies, gathered by NOAA NCEI: where and when each was taken, the medium (sea surface, water column, beach, sediment), the sampling method and mesh, the concentration and its unit, and the study's reference and DOI. NCEI gathers the studies; each sample's own lineage is its study, so two samples from one study are one voice.

sources.name: AGAGE methane (Ragged Point, Barbados and Mace Head, Ireland)
sources.licence: Free to use with the AGAGE data policy: cite the dataset DOI and Prinn et al. 2018 (doi:10.5194/essd-10-985-2018), and inform station PIs of use in publications.
sources.about: High-frequency in-situ methane from the AGAGE network, independent of NOAA's flask network. The second lineage the BCDE's global CH4 check is waiting on, and two of its stations sit on the Atlantic Rim: Ragged Point (Barbados) and Mace Head (Ireland). AGAGE data are a published cross-check on national inventories submitted to the UNFCCC. Needs a reader for the AGAGE monthly baseline files. Checked 13 November 2026.

sources.name: BIOS Bermuda Atlantic Time-series Study (BATS) and Hydrostation S
sources.licence: Open (US NSF-funded; BCO-DMO datasets CC BY 4.0), citing BATS/BIOS and the dataset DOI.
sources.about: Monthly ship-based profiles at 31°40'N 64°10'W since 1988 (Hydrostation S since 1954): temperature, salinity, oxygen, dissolved inorganic carbon, alkalinity, pH, nutrients, primary production. Bermuda's own ocean-carbon record and the anchor for the Bermuda Standard's ocean side; it gives Argo and Copernicus near Bermuda an independent ship-based lineage and is the reference any Atlantic blue or ocean carbon claim should be checked against. Served through BCO-DMO's ERDDAP; months to a year behind, so it is a reference, not a daily voice. Checked 13 November 2026.

sources.name: SOCAT Surface Ocean CO2 Atlas (v2026)
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0; cite the SOCAT data product and methods papers per socat.info/citing-socat.
sources.about: Quality-controlled surface-ocean CO2 fugacity (fCO2) from ships, moorings and drifters, 50+ million observations from 1957; released once a year (v2026 in June 2026, archived at NCEI, accession 0315110), with a gridded product. The community record behind the Global Carbon Budget's ocean sink. For the QEM: the reference for any claim about ocean CO2 uptake or acidification in an Atlantic Rim box, and the standard a future OCF ocean sensor's CO2 readings should agree with. Checked 13 November 2026.

sources.name: Global Mangrove Watch v4.1 (JAXA, Aberystwyth University, Wetlands International)
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, crediting Global Mangrove Watch (Aberystwyth University, soloEO, JAXA, Wetlands International, UNEP-WCMC).
sources.about: Annual 30 m mangrove extent and change for every mangrove country, 1985-2025 (v4.1.12, released August 2026), from Landsat, Sentinel-2 and JAXA L-band radar. The baseline for the blue carbon registry: a project's claimed mangrove area and its change are checked against it, and it is the first Gaia blue carbon layer. Zenodo carries the full v4.1 series; JAXA's raster download asks for a free registration. Checked 13 November 2026.

sources.name: Coastal Carbon Network Data Library (Smithsonian SERC)
sources.licence: Per dataset (mostly CC BY 4.0); cite the Coastal Carbon Library DOI (doi:10.25573/serc.21565671) and each original dataset.
sources.about: Open, disaggregated soil cores from tidal marshes, mangroves, tidal freshwater forests and seagrasses (about 15,000 cores), with depth series, dry bulk density, organic carbon and dating, on GitHub (smithsonian/ccn-data-library). For the registry: the independent check on a project's soil carbon stock, the pool that dominates blue carbon accounting and is easiest to overstate with a single national average. Checked 13 November 2026.

sources.name: Carbon Mapper methane and CO2 plumes
sources.licence: Free for non-commercial research and development; commercial use or redistribution needs Carbon Mapper's agreement (Terms of Use).
sources.about: Facility-scale methane and CO2 plumes with emission rates, from the Tanager satellites and airborne spectrometers, published within weeks of observation, via a public API (free account). An independent remote-sensing lineage to check Climate TRACE's asset estimates against: when both see the same facility, the QEM can triangulate an emission claim instead of carrying one model's word. Checked 13 November 2026.
